hypothesis: Prefilling the prompt on the GPU in batched chunks (weights read once per 8 tokens, tokens grouped per expert) instead of on the CPU removes the dominant cost of a short chat turn, with logits equal up to float summation order.
model: OLMoE-1B-7B-Instruct, Colibri int8-expert container (dense tensors FP16 on disk), 7.2 GB
command: make -C c olmoe-cuda-dll CUDA_ARCH=sm_89 && make -C c olmoe OLMOE_CUDA_DLL=1; arms alternate B,T,T,B,... after one warm-up pair: SNAP=<model> COLI_TEMP=0 COLI_OLMOE_CUDA_PREFILL=<0|1> PPL=1 ./olmoe 64 8 ref_p140.json (tok_s = the Speed line: 140-token prefill + 32 decode steps, so it is the end-to-end rate of a short turn); quality: greedy generate of 64 tokens compared between arms; verify: COLI_OLMOE_CUDA_VERIFY=1 PPL=1 on a 140-token (one chunk) and a 300-token (two chunks) prompt
